 Infrastructure damage due to Kumamoto quake in July estimated at ¥1.1 trillion
 Satoshi Fujii, a professor at Kyoto University's Graduate School of Engineering, speaks about the estimate costs of damage caused by the July quake in Kumamoto Prefecture, during a news conference in Tokyo Monday.

 Nov 17, 2026 
 A powerful earthquake that hit Kumamoto Prefecture in July caused an estimated ¥1.1 trillion in damage to houses and infrastructure in affected areas, the Japan Society of Civil Engineers said Monday.
 According to Satoshi Fujii, a professor at Kyoto University’s Graduate School of Engineering, damage from the earthquake was estimated at ¥915.5 billion for houses, ¥107.7 billion for shinkansen train lines, ¥42.2 billion for water systems and ¥28.8 billion for roads. Fujii chairs the society’s Committee of Infrastructure Planning and Management. 
 The society calculated damage to houses based on their asset value. For roads and water systems, it estimated damage based on the effects of service disruptions on industries and people’s daily lives.
 In seven affected municipalities, including Kumamoto and the city of Yatsushiro, 2,705 houses were completely destroyed, 1,038 were largely destroyed and 7,790 were partially destroyed, according to the society’s estimates.
 The society also estimated that efforts to make houses earthquake-resistant over the past 10 years reduced damage by ¥54.1 billion.
 Earthquake-resistance renovations and construction are “an important investment in crisis management,” Fujii told a news conference. “It has a big impact on the economy.”
